text: Est mihi purgatum crebro qui personet aurem:
translation: There is a voice that constantly rings in my well-rinsed ear:

text: condo et compono quae mox depromere possim.
translation: I store up and arrange what I may soon bring forth for use.

text: Restat ut his ego me ipse regam solerque elementis.
translation: It remains for me to rule and comfort myself with these first principles.

text: Est quadam prodire tenus, si non datur ultra.
translation: It is worth advancing to a certain point, even if one may not go further.

text: Feruet auaritia miseroque cupidine pectus:
translation: Does your heart burn with greed and wretched desire?

text: Vilius argentum est auro, uirtutibus aurum.
translation: Silver is cheaper than gold, and gold than virtue.

text: O ciues, ciues, quaerenda pecunia primum est;
translation: O citizens, citizens, money must be sought first;

text: idem eadem possunt horam durare probantes?
translation: Can the same men persist for a single hour in liking the same things?

text: nil ait esse prius, melius nil caelibe uita;
translation: He says nothing is finer, nothing better than a single life;

text: si non est, iurat bene solis esse maritis.
translation: If he is not married, he swears that only husbands are happy.

text: Cur ita crediderim, nisi quid te distinet, audi.
translation: Why I think so, unless something detains you, listen.

text: Antenor censet belli praecidere causam;
translation: Antenor advises cutting off the very cause of the war;

text: hunc amor, ira quidem communiter urit utrumque.
translation: Love burns the one, while anger inflames them both alike.

text: Vt iugulent hominem surgunt de nocte latrones;
translation: Robbers rise by night to cut a man's throat;

text: quod satis est cui contingit, nil amplius optet.
translation: Let him to whom enough has fallen wish for nothing more.

text: Sincerum est nisi uas, quodcumque infundis acescit.
translation: Unless the vessel is clean, whatever you pour in turns sour.

text: Sperne uoluptates; nocet empta dolore uoluptas.
translation: Scorn pleasures; pleasure bought with pain does harm.

text: Semper auarus eget; certum uoto pete finem.
translation: The greedy man is always in want; set a fixed limit to your desires.

text: Inuidus alterius macrescit rebus opimis;
translation: The envious man grows lean at the prosperity of another;

text: Bella quis et paces longum diffundit in aeuum?
translation: Who spreads wars and peace far into the coming ages?

text: grata superueniet quae non sperabitur hora.
translation: Welcome will come the hour that is not hoped for.

text: Si melius quid habes, arcesse uel imperium fer.
translation: If you have anything better, impart it; if not, submit to my rule.

text: Iamdudum splendet focus et tibi munda supellex.
translation: Long has my hearth been shining and the furniture made neat for you.

text: Quo mihi fortunam, si non conceditur uti?
translation: What good is fortune to me, if I am not permitted to use it?

text: Quo spectanda modo, quo sensu credis et ore?
translation: In what manner, with what mind and countenance do you think he should be viewed?

text: gaude quod spectant oculi te mille loquentem;
translation: Rejoice that a thousand eyes behold you as you speak;

text: ut cuique est aetas, ita quemque facetus adopta.
translation: According to each man's age, courteously adopt him as your own.

text: dum pueris omnis pater et matercula pallet.
translation: While every father and fond mother grows pale with anxiety for their children.

text: Non inuisa feres pueris munuscula paruis.
translation: You will bring small gifts that are not unwelcome to little children.

text: Tam teneor dono quam si dimittar onustus.
translation: I am as much obliged by the offer as if I were sent away laden with gifts.

text: Vt libet; haec porcis hodie comedenda relinques.
translation: As you please; you will leave them to be eaten by the swine today.

text: Prodigus et stultus donat quae spernit et odit;
translation: A prodigal and foolish man gives away what he despises and hates;

text: haec seges ingratos tulit et feret omnibus annis.
translation: Such a soil has borne, and will bear every year, a crop of ingrates.

text: dignum praestabo me etiam pro laude merentis.
translation: I will show myself worthy also in proportion to my benefactor's praise.

text: Hac ego si compellor imagine, cuncta resigno;
translation: If I am challenged by this parable, I resign everything;

text: inspice si possum donata reponere laetus.
translation: See whether I can cheerfully restore what was given to me.

text: Atride, magis apta tibi tua dona relinquam.
translation: Son of Atreus, I will leave your gifts to you, as they suit you better.

text: Metiri se quemque suo modulo ad pede uerum est.
translation: It is right that each man should measure himself by his own rule and foot.

text: ut placeat iuueni, percontare, utque cohorti.
translation: Inquire how he pleases the young prince, and how he suits the retinue.

text: Est ubi diuellat somnos minus inuida cura?
translation: Is there any place where envious care less rends our sleep?

text: pauper enim non est cui rerum suppetit usus.
translation: For he is not poor who has enough of things for his use.

text: Vilis amicorum est annona, bonis ubi quid dest.
translation: The price of friends is cheap when good men are in need of something.

text: Viribus uteris per cliuos, flumina, lamas.
translation: You will exert your strength across hills, rivers, and bogs.

text: Vade, uale, caue ne titubes mandataque frangas.
translation: Go, farewell; beware lest you stumble and break my commands.

text: Rure ego uiuentem, tu dicis in urbe beatum;
translation: I call him happy who lives in the country; you, him who lives in the city;

text: in culpa est animus, qui se non effugit umquam.
translation: The mind is at fault, which never escapes from itself.

text: Nunc age, quid nostrum concentum diuidat, audi.
translation: Come now, listen to what divides our harmony.

text: nec lusisse pudet, sed non incidere ludum.
translation: There is no shame in having played, but in not breaking off the play.

text: rident uicini glaebas et saxa mouentem.
translation: The neighbors laugh at me as I move clods and stones.

text: Cum seruis urbana diaria rodere mauis;
translation: You prefer to gnaw on city rations along with the slaves;

text: Optat ephippia bos piger, optat arare caballus;
translation: The lazy ox longs for the horse's trappings; the horse longs to plow;

text: quam scit uterque, libens, censebo, exerceat artem.
translation: My advice will be that each should willingly practice the art he knows.

text: rure meo possum quiduis perferre patique;
translation: On my country estate I can endure and put up with anything;

text: Tu recte uiuis, si curas esse quod audis.
translation: You live rightly if you take care to be what you are called.

text: Stultorum incurata pudor malus ulcera celat.
translation: It is the false shame of fools that hides unhealed ulcers.

text: detulerit fasces indigno, detrahet idem.
translation: He who has conferred the fasces on the unworthy will likewise take them away.

text: Oderunt peccare boni uirtutis amore;
translation: The good hate to sin from their love of virtue;

text: tu nihil admittes in te formidine poenae;
translation: You will commit no crime within yourself from fear of punishment;

text: sit spes fallendi, miscebis sacra profanis.
translation: Let there be hope of escaping notice, and you will mingle the sacred with the profane.

text: Vendere cum possis captiuum, occidere noli;
translation: When you can sell a captive, do not kill him;

text: Alter purpureum non expectabit amictum;
translation: The other will not wait for a purple cloak;

text: principibus placuisse uiris non ultima laus est.
translation: To have pleased leading men is not the lowest praise.

text: Sedit qui timuit ne non succederet; esto;
translation: He who feared lest he should not succeed sat still; so be it;

text: Credite, non ludo; crudeles, tollite claudum.
translation: Believe me, I am not joking; cruel men, lift up the lame!

text: Quaere peregrinum', uicinia rauca reclamat.
translation: 'Go look for a stranger!' the hoarse neighborhood cries back.

text: Virtus est medium uitiorum et utrimque reductum.
translation: Virtue is a mean between vices, removed from both extremes.

text: Dulcia inexpertis cultura potentis amici;
translation: Sweet to the inexperienced is the courting of a powerful friend;

text: quod superest aeui, siquid superesse uolunt di;
translation: May I have what remains of life, if the gods will that anything remain;

text: det uitam, det opes; aequum mi animum ipse parabo.
translation: Let Jove give life, let him give wealth; a tranquil mind I will provide for myself.

text: accipiat cingens materna tempora myrto;
translation: May he receive them, binding his temples with his mother's myrtle;

text: illius immensae ruperunt horrea messes.
translation: His boundless harvests have burst the granaries.

text: tunc alnos primum fluuii sensere cauatas;
translation: Then first the rivers felt the hollowed alders;

text: incipe et ad medias sementem extende pruinas.
translation: Begin, and extend your sowing right up to the midwinter frosts.

text: ter pater exstructos disiecit fulmine montis.
translation: Three times the Father shattered the piled-up mountains with his thunderbolt.

text: nudus ara, sere nudus. hiems ignaua colono:
translation: Plow lightly clad, sow lightly clad; winter is an idle time for the farmer.

text: nunc nemora ingenti uento, nunc litora plangunt.
translation: Now the woods, now the shores wail with the mighty wind.

text: tam multa in tectis crepitans salit horrida grando.
translation: So thick the bristling hail leaps rattling on the roofs.

text: Hactenus aruorum cultus et sidera caeli;
translation: Thus far the tillage of the fields and the stars of heaven;

text: Principio arboribus uaria est natura creandis.
translation: First of all, nature is varied in the ways of producing trees.

text: sunt alii, quos ipse uia sibi repperit usus:
translation: There are others that experience itself has found out along its course:

text: Nec modus inserere atque oculos imponere simplex.
translation: Nor is the manner of grafting and budding one and the same.

text: Nec uero terrae ferre omnes omnia possunt.
translation: Nor indeed can all soils bear all things.

text: hic uer adsiduum atque alienis mensibus aestas:
translation: Here spring is perpetual, and summer shines in months not her own:

text: bis grauidae pecudes, bis pomis utilis arbos.
translation: Twice a year the cattle teem, twice the tree serves with fruit.

text: an mare quod supra memorem, quodque adluit infra?
translation: Or shall I tell of the sea that washes it above, and that which washes it below?

text: Nunc quo quamque modo possis cognoscere dicam.
translation: Now I will tell how you may recognize the nature of each soil.

text: Forsitan et scrobibus quae sint fastigia quaeras.
translation: Perhaps too you may ask what depth is best for the trenches.

text: ausim uel tenui uitem committere sulco;
translation: I would dare to entrust the vine even to a shallow furrow;

text: infelix superat foliis oleaster amaris.
translation: Only the barren wild olive survives with its bitter leaves.

text: et dubitant homines serere atque impendere curam?
translation: And do men still hesitate to plant and bestow their care?

text: condit opes alius defossoque incubat auro;
translation: Another hoards up wealth and broods over buried gold;

text: agricola incuruo terram dimouit aratro:
translation: The farmer has cleaved the earth with his curved plow:

text: cetera nec feturae habilis nec fortis aratris.
translation: At other times she is neither fit for breeding nor strong for the plow.

text: semper erunt quarum mutari corpora malis:
translation: There will always be some cattle whose stock you would wish to improve:

text: Nec non et pecori est idem dilectus equino:
translation: Moreover, the horse's herd requires the very same care in selection:

text: densa iuba, et dextro iactata recumbit in armo;
translation: Thick is his mane, and tossed, it rests upon his right shoulder;

text: deficit, abde domo, nec turpi ignosce senectae.
translation: When he fails, keep him at home, and spare his blameless old age.

text: tantus amor laudum, tantae est uictoria curae.
translation: So great is their love of praise, so dear to them is victory.

text: Post partum cura in uitulos traducitur omnis;
translation: After birth, all care is transferred to the calves;

text: cetera pascuntur uiridis armenta per herbas:
translation: The rest of the herds graze at large through the green pastures:

text: ille uolat simul arua fuga simul aequora uerrens.
translation: He flies, sweeping simultaneously over the fields and the sea in his flight.

text: scilicet ante omnis furor est insignis equarum;
translation: Assuredly, above all others, the frenzy of mares is remarkable;

text: hic labor, hinc laudem fortes sperate coloni.
translation: Here lies the labor; hence, brave farmers, hope for praise.

text: densior hinc suboles, hinc largi copia lactis;
translation: Hence comes a thicker offspring, hence a generous supply of milk;

text: interea toto non setius aere ningit:
translation: Meanwhile, no less relentlessly, it snows through all the sky:

text: continuoque greges uillis lege mollibus albos.
translation: From the outset, choose flocks with soft and snowy fleeces.

text: Morborum quoque te causas et signa docebo.
translation: I will also teach you the causes and signs of diseases.

text: haec ante exitium primis dant signa diebus:
translation: In the first days before death, they give these signs:

text: Alter erit maculis auro squalentibus ardens;
translation: The one will be fiery, gleaming with scales of gold;

text: Ut binae regum facies, ita corpora plebis.
translation: Just as there are two types of kings, so too are the bodies of the common bees.

text: Fervet opus, redolentque thymo fragrantia mella.
translation: The work glows, and the fragrant honey smells of thyme.

text: Omnibus una quies operum, labor omnibus unus:
translation: For all there is one rest from toil, for all one time of labor:

text: fit sonitus, mussantque oras et limina circum.
translation: A buzzing arises, and they hum around the borders and thresholds.

text: tantus amor florum et generandi gloria mellis.
translation: So great is their love of flowers and their glory in making honey.

text: Unde nova ingressus hominum experientia cepit?
translation: Whence did this new experience of men take its beginning?

text: Omine quo firmans animum sic incipit ipsa:
translation: Cheering her heart with this omen, she herself thus begins:

text: Sternunt se somno diversae in litore phocae.
translation: Seals scatter and lay themselves down to sleep along the shore.

text: Non te nullius exercent numinis irae;
translation: It is the wrath of no slight deity that pursues you;

text: Iamque pedem referens casus evaserat omnes;
translation: And now, retracing his steps, he had escaped every peril;

text: Eurydicen toto referebant flumine ripae".
translation: 'Eurydice!' the banks echoed back along the whole stream.

text: Nate, licet tristes animo deponere curas.
translation: My son, you may lay aside the sad cares from your heart.

text: namque dabunt veniam votis irasque remittent.
translation: For they will grant pardon to your prayers and lay aside their wrath.

text: Sed modus orandi qui sit, prius ordine dicam.
translation: But first I will tell you in order what the manner of supplication is.

text: Haud mora; continuo matris praecepta facessit;
translation: Without delay, he straightway carries out his mother's bidding;
